title: Keep your coding agent on task when you add requests
summary: A developer wrote a skill that makes Codex and Claude Code finish the current job before new requests; one live Codex test passed all 10 checks, they report.
agent_role: The agent tracks one active task, applies corrections right away, and queues new requests until the current work is checked. The human can still pause, cancel or reprioritize.
outcome: Author reports one live Codex run passed all 10 recorded checks; a second stop test passed 11 of 12, with slow cancellation.
what_they_did: A developer wrote a set of standing instructions, called a skill, for Codex and Claude Code. When you send a new message mid-task, the agent decides whether it is a correction, a question, or a new job. New jobs wait in a queue until the current one is finished and checked.
how_it_went: The author reports a live Codex test where a second request arrived mid-task. The first task was finished and checked before the second began, passing all 10 checks. A stop test passed 11 of 12, but cancelling took about 35 seconds.
worth_knowing: It is only instructions, so it cannot force the agent to comply. Claude Code was not part of the live tests.
prompt: For the rest of this session, follow this rule. Keep one active task at a time. If I send a new, unrelated request while you work, add it to a queue and tell me it is queued. Then finish and check the current task before starting it. If my message corrects the current task, apply it right away. If I ask for status, answer briefly and continue. If I say pause, cancel or stop, do that at once and don't start queued work. Show me the queue whenever it changes. Start with: [your first task].

curation.rationale: A shared skill that changes how coding agents handle new requests mid-task, backed by one documented live test with honest limits; narrow and meta, but reproducible.
